summary: The previous bundle improved batching and retained rendering, but the runtime workbench is still primarily DOM/SVG, the toolbox is not production-ready, and shared canvas code remains monolithic.

gaps.title: Runtime workbench is still DOM/SVG instead of real canvas
gaps.why_it_matters: Dense graphs still pay DOM/SVG composition costs and cannot reach true canvas scalability.

gaps.title: Move flow still reloads the full surface after batch persistence
gaps.why_it_matters: Batch persistence gains are partially lost because ordinary drag commits still force expensive full rebuilds.

gaps.title: View-state persistence remains too eager in ProjectStructure and PromptFactory
gaps.why_it_matters: InteractiveServer latency, DB writes, and refresh churn stay on the hot path.

gaps.title: Overlay input ownership is incomplete
gaps.why_it_matters: Toolbox/floating-window interactions can leak into zoom, selection, or pan handlers.

gaps.title: Toolbox accordion and layout are still not in the requested Visual Studio-like state
gaps.why_it_matters: Primary authoring UX is broken or inconsistent with the requested behavior.

gaps.title: CanvasLib runtime, preview, and legacy concerns are still mixed together
gaps.why_it_matters: Developers cannot easily see which code is runtime-critical versus preview or legacy reference code.

gaps.title: Asset loading is duplicated across app shells
gaps.why_it_matters: Manual includes drift and make large refactors easier to break.

gaps.title: Export path still depends on DOM clone instead of renderer-owned composition
gaps.why_it_matters: A true canvas runtime needs a true canvas export pipeline to avoid misleading or brittle captures.
